topic_and_scope: This document evaluates the clinical utility of left atrial (LA) strain via 2D speckle tracking echocardiography in HFpEF, highlighting its potential for diagnosis, phenotyping, and risk stratification, while underscoring the need for standardization, normative data, and multicenter validation before routine adoption.
main_themes: LA strain as a diagnostic, phenotypic, and prognostic tool in HFpEF, with emphasis on reservoir, conduit, and pump components.
Technical and methodological variability in LA strain/GLS measurement across vendors, imaging views, and loading conditions.
Need for standardized protocols, normative reference values, and large-scale prospective validation to enable clinical integration.
main_findings: LA strain correlates with LV filling pressures and diastolic dysfunction and has independent prognostic value for major adverse cardiovascular events and atrial fibrillation in HFpEF, offering information beyond traditional LV function measurements.

HFpEF is a heterogeneous syndrome; LV longitudinal function–driven phenotypes (e.g., HFpEF-rLS) and LA strain–based phenotyping provide deeper insights into underlying pathophysiology, aiding risk stratification and potential targeted management.

key_gaps.description: There is no universally accepted standardization for LA strain measurement across vendors, views, and analysis platforms, nor widely established cut-offs or normative reference values.

Evidence validating LAS/GLS prognostic value in HFpEF is largely cross-sectional or derived from small cohorts; there is a critical need for large, multicenter, prospective studies to confirm predictive utility and inform guidelines.

future_directions.title: Standardize LA strain measurement protocols and establish vendor-independent cut-offs
future_directions.rationale: The review identifies substantial inter-vendor and viewing variability in LA strain results and notes the lack of standardized cut-offs. A formal process should convene expert panels to reach consensus on acquisition views (e.g., apical 4-chamber vs 2-chamber), segmentation, reference points, and analysis algorithms. A multicenter study with a central core lab across multiple vendors should derive robust normative ranges stratified by age and sex, followed by validation in independent cohorts. The outcome would be widely disseminated guidelines and publicly available reference values to support clinical decision-making.

future_directions.title: Launch large, multicenter prospective cohorts to validate LAS/GLS prognostic value in HFpEF
future_directions.rationale: Current evidence linking LAS/GLS to outcomes in HFpEF is limited by design and sample size. A prospective study across diverse populations with standardized imaging, centralized analysis, and long follow-up should assess incremental prognostic value for MACE, HF hospitalizations, and mortality beyond NT-proBNP and conventional echocardiography. This work should also quantify the impact of loading conditions and rhythm status. Results would inform risk stratification models and potential guideline updates.

future_directions.title: Develop an LAS-based HFpEF phenotyping framework integrating LA strain components and LV GLS
future_directions.rationale: HFpEF is heterogeneous, with subgroups like HFpEF-rLS reflecting contractile dysfunction and fibrosis. A framework combining LARS, LA conduit strain, LA pump strain, and LV GLS, plus MRI-derived fibrosis where available, could define clinically meaningful phenogroups. Cluster analyses in large cohorts should link phenotypes to outcomes and treatment responses, enabling more precise patient stratification and personalized therapy approaches.

future_directions.title: Define LAS thresholds for risk stratification and AF prediction in HFpEF and combine with LVFP markers
future_directions.rationale: Identifying specific LAS cut-offs for predicting adverse events and AF risk would facilitate clinical decision-making. Studies should useReceiver Operating Characteristic/generalized linear models and decision-curve analyses to establish thresholds for reservoir, conduit, and pump strain, and assess their additive value to LV filling pressure estimates (PAWP) and NT-proBNP. Prospective validation in diverse populations is essential to ensure generalizability.

future_directions.title: Characterize and correct for rhythm-related effects on LAS measurements
future_directions.rationale: AF and irregular rhythms are prevalent in HFpEF and degrade strain accuracy. Research should quantify measurement variability across rhythm states, develop rhythm-specific corrections or cycle-averaged metrics, and validate alternative indices when rhythm is non-sinus. This work will enable reliable LAS use in real-world HFpEF populations.

future_directions.title: Head-to-head comparison of 2D STE LAS versus cardiac MRI–based LA strain
future_directions.rationale: While STE is widely used, MRI-based LA strain may offer higher reproducibility or complementary insights (e.g., fibrosis correlation). A prospective, cross-modality study should compare prognostic accuracy, reproducibility, and feasibility across settings, informing guidelines about when MRI adds clinical value and cost-effective use of imaging resources.

future_directions.title: Implement automated, clinically integrated LAS workflows with quality assurance
future_directions.rationale: To translate LAS into practice, automated analysis pipelines with robust QA, user-friendly interfaces, and training programs are needed. Pilot implementations should assess workflow time, inter-operator variability, learning curves, and impact on clinical decision-making. Economic evaluations and integration with electronic health records will support adoption and reimbursement considerations.
